meaning:
ἄκανθα, -ης, ἡ
(ἀκή, a point), [in LXX chiefly for קוֹץ, also for סִיר, שַׁיִת, etc. ;]
a prickly plant, thorn, brier; in NT always pl.: Mat.7:16 13:7,22 27:29, Mrk.4:7,18, Luk.6:44 8:7,14, Jhn.19:2, Heb.6:8 (see MM, VGT, see word).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: By their fruits you will know them. Do you gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
Others fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
For each tree is known by its own fruit. For people don’t gather figs from thorns, nor do they gather grapes from a bramble bush.
The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown, and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.
but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is rejected and near being cursed, whose end is to be burned.
